[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC sase-n4[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Auto-disable LLM providers on usage-limit errors[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]When a sase agent fails because its LLM provider reported a [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]usage/quota limit, sase recognizes that failure, temporarily [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]disables just that provider (honoring the reset time the provider [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]itself reported when one is available), stops wasting retries on [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]it, and tells the user what happened with a rich notification. [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]Defaults work out of the box for every shipped provider, and users [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]can extend or replace the patterns and durations from config.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]4[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]3[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Usage-limit detection core[/bold #D7AFFF]                                    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]detect[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]detect: add the `llm_provider.usage_limit` config section, its JSON [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]schema, the `llm_default_usage_limit_config` plugin hook, evidence-based[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]built-in patterns for every shipped provider, and the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]normalize/match/exclude plus reset-hint parsing logic, with a regression[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]corpus of real captured provider messages.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Runtime disable and retry precedence[/bold #D7AFFF]                          [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]enforce[dim] · [dim][/dim]after detect[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]enforce: call detection from the LLM invocation error paths, write the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]temporary provider disable through the existing Rust-backed store with a[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]structured source, make a usage-limit failure take precedence over the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]retry loop so agents stop sleeping through futile waits, and record [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]telemetry.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Rich usage-limit notification[/bold #D7AFFF]                                 [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]notify[dim] · [dim][/dim]after enforce[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]notify: add a notification sender that reports which provider was [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]disabled, for how long and until when, what the provider actually said, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and which agent tripped it, with once-per-disable-window dedup.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Surface the disable reason and document the feature[/bold #D7AFFF]           [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]surface[dim] · [dim][/dim]after enforce[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]surface: render automatic versus manual provenance in the Models panel [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and the top-bar provider-disable indicator, and document the new config [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]section in the default config and user docs.[/#D7D7AF]
